chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bakir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There are four [people] for whom the chastisement is quickest: A man to whom you do good, yet he repays your good with evil; a man whom you do not oppress, yet he oppresses you; a man with whom you make a pledge, where your intention is to fulfill it while his intention is to betray you; and a man who maintains ties of kinship, yet they cut them off.
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of people who receive quick punishment according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights four archetypes of injustice that trigger immediate divine retribution, emphasizing the spiritual gravity of reciprocal betrayal, unprovoked aggression, and the specific sin of severing kinship (*qat' al-rahim*) despite one's own efforts. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in social relations, particularly the obligation of maintaining family ties even when others fail to reciprocate, a theme deeply rooted in the concept of *'adl* (divine justice).
